newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Jianshe sees 75 pct fall in '96 net.
newsitem.headline: China's Jianshe sees 75 pct fall in '96 net.

text.p: Shenzhen-listed North Jianshe Motorcycle Co Ltd estimates a 75 percent drop in net earnings for 1996 on sharply lower sales caused by stiffening competition, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
The firm expected a net profit of 70 million yuan or 0.15 yuan per share for 1996, down from 288.71 million yuan in 1995, the spokesman told Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Precise figures would not be released to the public until an audit is completed, the official said.
The share closed on Wednesday at HK$4.00, dipping HK$0.03 from Tuesday.
The lower earnings were due to sharpening competition in China's motorcycle market where supply far exceeded demand, he said.
The official said the firm sold about 630,000 motorbikes in 1996, down 29 percent compared with 890,000 in 1995 and it has lowered its sale prices by an average 10 percent since October 1995.
Despite the plunge in earnings, Jianshe expected to post a 40 percent year-on-year jump in net profits for 1997 when efforts to develop new models and promotions pay off, he said.
The company's 1996 interim after-tax profits fell 65 percent to 48.31 million yuan from 137.66 million yuan in the year-earlier period, under international accounting standards.
In the interim report, Jianshe said it had lowered its output target for 1996 to 700,977 units from the original 950,000 units, and its sales goal to 2.49 billion yuan from 2.98 billion yuan.
Earnings per share reached 0.60 yuan in 1995, up 30.43 percent from 0.46 yuan in 1994.
